editorial:
Imagine having a dad who is a big-shot movie producer but cannot even talk to his own kid. That is exactly what you get here. You will meet a wealthy father and his rebellious teenage son who just cannot see eye to eye. Things go from bad to worse when the boy gets into a fight at a movie theater. Instead of helping him work through it, the dad pushes him away, and the whole situation spirals. It feels like a tense family argument that never ends, and you can really feel the frustration building up as the story moves along.

What really makes this work is the acting, as both leads feel like real people you might know. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are used to modern action movies. However, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you love old-school dramas about family secrets and growing pains, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a quiet movie night.
endingExplained: At the end, the father finally stops acting like a boss and starts acting like a dad. He realizes that his money and fame did not make his son happy. After a big emotional blowout, they finally have an honest conversation. They both admit where they went wrong and decide to fix their relationship. It ends on a hopeful note, showing that talking things out is the only way to heal a broken family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic family dramas and character studies.
